[USER] The user is looking for advice on fertilizing their herbs.  
[USER] The user has been using a general-purpose fertilizer for their herbs.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] General-purpose fertilizers may not provide the nutrients required for herbs.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] High nitrogen levels in general-purpose fertilizers can promote leaf growth at the expense of flavor and essential oil production in herbs.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Herbs prefer a slightly acidic to neutral soil pH (around 6.0-7.0).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Herbs require specific micronutrients like iron, zinc, and manganese, which might be lacking in general-purpose fertilizers.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended N-P-K ratios for herbs include 5-5-5 or 10-10-10.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested fertilizers for herbs include:  
- Miracle-Gro Shake 'n Feed All Purpose Plant Food  
- Espoma Organic Herb Tone Fertilizer  
- E.B. Stone Organics Herb & Vegetable Fertilizer  
- Fish emulsion or compost tea  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Fertilize herbs sparingly and test soil periodically to determine pH and nutrient levels.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Watering should be consistent but not waterlogged.  
[USER] The user has been using tap water for their herb plants.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tap water is generally okay but may contain impurities, chemicals, and minerals that affect herb health and flavor.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Pros of tap water include convenience and cost-effectiveness.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cons of tap water include chlorine and chloramines, mineral buildup, and potential pH imbalance.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Pros of rainwater include being natural, chemical-free, and typically pH balanced.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cons of rainwater include availability and storage/maintenance issues.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Pros of filtered water include removal of impurities and consistent quality.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cons of filtered water include additional cost and maintenance.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommendations for using tap water include letting it sit for 24 hours, using a water conditioner, and monitoring pH.  
[USER] The user has been having issues with pests on their African Violet, noticing tiny white insects on the underside of the leaves.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The tiny white insects are likely mealybugs, which feed on plant sap and can cause yellowing leaves and stunted growth.
